name: the Jardin des Plantes
title: Ancient Trees in the Jardin des Plantes, Paris: 6 to Find
meta_description: Paris's second oldest tree, a 1636 black locust, shares the old royal garden with Jussieu's 1734 cedar, Vaillant's pistachio and two planes from 1785.
intro: The second oldest tree in Paris grows in the Jardin des Plantes, a black locust Vespasien Robin planted in 1636 from a cutting of his father's tree, which still stands two kilometres away. It went into the royal garden of medicinal plants in its first years, and the trees that followed read like a roll call of the scientists who worked there. Sébastien Vaillant's pistachio, planted in 1702 or sown in 1704 depending on whose date you take, is the tree he is said to have used to show that flowers have sexes, which he set out in a lecture in 1717. Bernard de Jussieu brought a cedar of Lebanon from England in 1734, by legend carrying it the last stretch in his hat, and it is now the oldest of its species in France. Two planes date from 1785, under Buffon. One is an oriental plane, the last of three he planted; the other a London plane whose roots erosion has laid bare on the labyrinth hill. The bur oak by the Cuvier gate came in 1811, after the Revolution had turned the garden into the national natural history museum. Entry is free.
